title: Fix the Swapped Arguments
description: The program should compute base raised to the power of exponent using a helper function. Fix the bug.
expectedBehavior: compute_power_of_two(2) should compute 2 raised to the power of 2, so it should print 4; more importantly, calling compute_power_of_two(3) should raise 2 to the power of 3 (8), not 3 to the power of 2.
actualProblem: compute_power_of_two is supposed to always raise 2 to the power of n, but it calls power(n, 2), which computes n ** 2 instead of 2 ** n — the arguments are passed in the wrong order for the intended meaning.
explanation: When calling a function with positional arguments, the order matters — power(n, 2) and power(2, n) compute completely different things. The fix passes 2 as the base and n as the exponent, matching the function's intended purpose.
